papers.title_en: FAVR: Flow-Aware Visual Residual Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.authors: Qixuan Wu, Xiaole Yang, Yuguang Yang, Canyu Chen, Linlin Yang, Haixia Pan, Guodong Guo, Baochang Zhang
papers.evidence: 为冻结的视觉-语言-动作操作策略提供流感知视觉条件化
papers.tldr: 预训练视频表征蕴含丰富时序信息，但难以有效融入视觉-语言-动作策略。FAVR以轻量框架为冻结VLA提供流感知视觉条件：用线性TTT维护紧凑时序状态，并在流式动作生成中检索动作条件视觉特征。它利用冻结动作头的仿射结构，将通道选择建模为盒约束优化并用FISTA求解。仅需1.74–2.19M可训练参数和5000步适配，便在RoboTwin 2.0上将LingBot-VLA成功率从87.12%提升至90.04%。
papers.abstract_en: Pretrained video representations provide rich temporal information for robotic manipulation, yet effectively integrating them into existing vision-language-action (VLA) policies remains challenging. We present Flow-Aware Visual Residual Alignment (FAVR), a lightweight framework for flow-aware visual conditioning of frozen VLA policies. FAVR maintains a compact temporal visual state through linear Test-Time Training (TTT) and retrieves action-conditioned visual features throughout flow-based action generation. By exploiting the affine structure of the frozen action head, we explicitly characterize how injected visual features influence predicted action velocities and formulate flow-aware channel selection as a box-constrained optimization problem. We develop a FISTA-based solver for joint gate optimization and derive an efficient closed-form approximation through diagonalization and rescaling. With only 1.74-2.19M trainable parameters and 5,000 adaptation steps, FAVR improves pretrained VLA policies across benchmarks. On RoboTwin 2.0, FAVR improves LingBot-VLA from 87.12% to 90.04% under clean conditions and from 86.88% to 89.38% under randomized conditions. A controlled ablation on five RoboTwin tasks further shows that flow-aware gating increases average success from 72.0% with a gate shared across flow steps to 82.0%, demonstrating the benefit of adapting visual conditioning throughout action generation.

papers.title_en: TempQuant: Learning Adaptive Temperatures for Quantized Language Models
papers.authors: Mukund Athmaram, Liang Ma, Manoj Rao
papers.evidence: 为量化语言模型学习自适应温度
papers.tldr: 量化会改变大模型下一词分布，使采样温度对量化模型的影响远大于全精度模型。TempQuant通过无标签学习量化模型的温度与top-p，使其下一词概率更接近全精度模型，并支持全局与逐token两种粒度。在3-bit Qwen3-4B上，全局TempQuant将MATH准确率从34%提升到51%。该工作表明量化模型不应照搬全精度采样配置，自适应采样可显著恢复性能。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models are increasingly deployed at low precision, yet quantization can degrade their performance. We study how quantization interacts with decoding settings such as the sampling temperature and top-p by examining how it distorts the model's next-token probabilities. Measuring entropy during generation across deployed temperatures, we find that quantization warms the model on average, and that temperature matters much more for the performance of a quantized model than for its full-precision counterpart. Because quantization and temperature both shape the next-token distribution, we investigate how much the sampling settings can undo what quantization changes, through our method TempQuant, which learns the quantized model's temperature and top-p to bring its next-token probabilities closer to the full-precision model's. We learn these settings at two granularities. The first is a single global setting per requested temperature, which finds nearly the same temperatures that tuning on labeled answers would, without any labels. Model cards typically recommend sampling a quantized model with the same settings as its full-precision counterpart, while we find that different settings can substantially improve its accuracy. On 3-bit Qwen3-4B, for example, global TempQuant raises MATH accuracy from 34% under the configuration recommended for Qwen's quantized releases to 51%. The second sets the temperature and top-p for every token, motivated by our finding that tokens whose rankings flip under quantization tend to need warming, while tokens whose rankings are preserved tend to need cooling. When quantization degrades accuracy substantially, TempQuant recovers much of it, and when degradation is lighter, it still brings the quantized model's behavior closer to the full-precision model's.

papers.evidence: 从示范中学习语言条件进度场梯度的机器人策略
papers.tldr: 机器人操作需要把任务描述转化为具体动作，但直接拟合进度值并不能保证动作梯度与专家命令一致。PPP 学习语言条件标量进度场，将其与共享世界模型组合，在固定参考命令处读取动作梯度；连续命令用学习正增益缩放，离散命令用有限差分，形成无需独立动作头或迭代搜索的混合策略。训练时以模仿学习诱导命令，并用双反向传播塑造局部控制几何，演示时序仅用于校准观测状态的进度值。仿真与真实机器人实验表明，在共享架构下 PPP 优于行为克隆，且校准后的进度值可用于执行中进度监控。
papers.abstract_en: A task specifies how the world should change, while a policy specifies what the robot should do. We introduce Progress Predicts Policy (PPP), which learns a language-conditioned scalar field through the commands induced by its differential. We obtain action conditioning by composing a latent progress field with a shared world model and read its action gradient at a fixed reference command. Continuous commands scale this gradient by a learned positive gain, while discrete commands use finite differences of the same scalar. This yields a hybrid policy without a separate action head or iterative search. Fitting demonstration progress values alone does not ensure that action gradients align with expert commands. PPP trains the induced commands by imitation and uses double backpropagation for the continuous gradient readout to shape the field's local control geometry. Demonstration timing calibrates field values on observed states without additional annotation. The continuous readout remains learnable without progress labels but these timing-derived targets support progress monitoring during execution. Experiments in simulated and real robot manipulation show that PPP outperforms behavioral cloning under a shared architecture.

papers.title_en: Body Schema Policy: Body as the Vision-Action Interface for Efficient Robot Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Lechen Zhang, Chenyuan Chen, Muxin Zhou, Zewen He, Yoshihiko Nakamura
papers.evidence: 面向机器人移动操作的身体中心视觉-动作模仿学习策略
papers.tldr: 现有全身移动操作策略依赖数十亿参数和任务微调，效率受限。BSP将身体图式嵌入视觉-动作接口，在运动树上组织关节与连杆token，用螺旋运动传递特征，并让身体部位查询自身视觉证据以条件化动作去噪。在九个模拟G1任务上，BSP匹配Ψ0且参数少75倍，成功率近翻倍Diffusion Policy，动作生成更快，并在真实G1与Fetch上验证。该工作以紧凑的身体图式归纳偏置实现高效机器人全身移动操作。
papers.abstract_en: Currently, robots can learn whole-body loco-manipulation through scale: the strongest policies have billions of parameters and still need task-specific fine-tuning. Humans have limited processing capacity, yet learn and act efficiently through a body schema that organizes what they see and how they move. We introduce Body Schema Policy (BSP), an imitation learning policy that builds such a schema into the vision-action interface. Its latent body schema places joint and link tokens on the robot's kinematic tree, where learned screw motions carry features between links. Through body-queried vision, each body part retrieves its own visual evidence, which conditions the denoising of its actions. With this inductive bias, BSP returns an action chunk faster than any policy we compare. Compact, body-specific visual readouts also emerge without spatial supervision: manipulation commands depend strongly on task objects, while locomotion commands respond more broadly to the scene. On nine simulated Unitree G1 whole-body tasks, BSP matches the $Ψ_0$ humanoid foundation model with $75\times$ fewer parameters and nearly doubles Diffusion Policy's success. The same holds on a real G1 and a Fetch mobile manipulator.

papers.authors: Xuanwei Liu, Guipu Cao, Zhongyi Luo, Jiafei Duan
papers.evidence: 面向自回归视觉-语言-动作策略的双臂动作标记化。
papers.tldr: 双臂操作中，现有动作分词器常把双臂动作拼接为单一向量，导致共享运动模式与跨臂依赖需由策略隐式学习。BiCAT 让双臂共享运动表示，并通过对称交叉注意力与联合解码器，使每条臂的 token 以另一条臂为条件。策略并行预测每条臂的全部 token，先生成左臂再条件生成右臂。在十个 RoboTwin 2.0 仿真任务和六个真实任务上，BiCAT 成功率最高，仿真平均提升 17.6 个百分点，动作块仅需 40.5 毫秒。
papers.abstract_en: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models predict discrete action tokens with the next-token objective of their vision-language backbone, so the action tokenizer defines the interface between the policy and the robot. In bimanual manipulation, the two arms share a repertoire of movements yet coordinate through complementary roles, and an action representation should capture both. However, most existing tokenizers encode both arms as a single concatenated action vector, in which motion patterns common to the two arms are not shared and cross-arm dependencies remain entangled within each token. The policy must therefore learn both aspects implicitly. We propose Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization (BiCAT), which shares one motion representation across arms while conditioning each arm's tokens on its partner through symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder. The policy then predicts all tokens of each arm in parallel, generating the left arm first and the right arm conditioned on it. Across ten RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and six real-world tasks on three embodiments, BiCAT achieves the highest success among the compared tokenizers. In simulation, it improves mean success by 17.6 percentage points over the strongest of eight baselines, with the largest gains on tasks that require close coordination between the arms, while requiring only 40.5 ms per action chunk. These results suggest that the action tokenizer is a natural place to model bimanual coordination.

papers.title_en: LoRN: Low-Rank Noise Steering for Generative Robot Policies
papers.authors: Wei Liu, Abrar Anwar, Huihua Zhao, Soha Pouya, Yan Chang
papers.evidence: 生成式机器人策略的低秩噪声引导
papers.tldr: 生成式机器人策略可通过选择初始噪声提升表现，但现有噪声引导难以扩展到世界动作模型的高维噪声输入。LoRN 训练小型引导 actor，在固定低秩随机投影上选择方向，并用范数控制使噪声保持高斯典型尺度，从而同时引导视频与动作输入。在三个世界动作模型和十个模型-任务对上，视频引导平均成功率较基础策略提升26.2个百分点，高于DSRL的7.1个百分点；仿真训练的引导 actor 还能零额外真实训练迁移到三项真实双臂操作任务。
papers.abstract_en: Noise steering improves pretrained generative robot policies by learning to select their initial noise without updating model weights. We find that actions in the evaluated world-action models are more sensitive to video noise than action noise, making video noise an expressive input for steering. However, the noise-steering methods we evaluate, in their published forms, struggle to scale to the high-dimensional noise inputs of large policy classes such as world-action models. We introduce Low-Rank Noise Steering (LoRN), a reinforcement learning method that scales noise steering to world-action models. A small steering actor selects a direction through a fixed low-rank random projection, while our norm-controlled construction keeps the resulting noise near the typical scale of a Gaussian sample. This separates the actor's control dimension from the full noise dimension, enabling steering of both video and action inputs. Across three world-action models and ten model-task pairs, video steering improves average success by 26.2 percentage points over the base policy, compared with 7.1 points for DSRL action steering. For smaller action policies, the same construction achieves comparable final success while generally improving early-training success. Steering actors trained in simulation also transfer to three physical bimanual manipulation tasks across two base policies, without additional real-world training.

papers.title_en: ZERITH V2.5: From Predictive Power to Policy Learnability
papers.authors: Chenxi Han, Ruby, Epoch, Orion, Luke, Bin, Dusk, Lyra, Cal, Alvin, Hubert, Alex, Jiahe Han, Tao Zhang, Hang Liu, Shoujie Li, Yizhe Li, Bokui Chen, Houde Liu, Guoping Pan, Yi Cheng
papers.evidence: 动作策略读取视频生成特征的视频-动作模型用于操作控制
papers.tldr: 视频生成模型具备预测先验，但动作策略如何有效利用这些先验仍不清楚。ZERITH V2.5 让动作策略读取视频生成模型中间特征，并在固定示范与更新次数下比较不同预测训练监督方式。实验发现多噪声级适配带来大幅提升，仅部署噪声级适配无效；增益需保留在视频模型中而非只初始化策略。该工作表明目标域预测适配可改善控制，并在多个仿真与真实机器人任务上验证。
papers.abstract_en: When humans learn to manipulate an unfamiliar object, they may already be able to anticipate how its state will change while still being unable to control it skillfully. This gap between prediction and control motivates us to study how the priors acquired by video generation models can be used effectively by an action policy. We present ZERITH V2.5, a video-action model (VAM) in which the action policy reads intermediate features of a video generation model, and use it to study, under fixed demonstrations and a fixed total number of updates, what kind of predictive training improves subsequent action learning.   We find that the way video predictive training is supervised affects subsequent action learning. In our experiments, adapting at many noise levels yields a large gain, while adapting only at the noise level used at deployment yields none. Weight-transfer experiments further show that the gain stays with the adapted weights when they remain in the video generation model and disappears when they are used only to initialize the action policy. Initial loss and gradient measurements at the start of joint training indicate that target-domain predictive training gives the video model a better starting state, making subsequent joint learning of prediction and action easier. Under matched data and training budgets, predictive adaptation improves control. We evaluate the complete policy on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, Meta-World MT50, and real-robot tasks.

papers.title_en: LaST1.0: A Unified Latent World-Action Model with Control-Centric SpatioTemporal Reasoning
papers.authors: Hao Chen, Xuheng Zhang, Zhuangzhe Wu, Jiaming Liu, Shaobo Zhang, Jialin Gao, Zhonghao Yan, Di Wu, Sixiang Chen, Peng Jia, Chi-Wing Fu, Shanghang Zhang, Pheng-Ann Heng
papers.evidence: 面向机器人操作控制的统一潜在世界-动作模型
papers.tldr: 现有世界-动作模型多以重建未来视频为目标，容易把容量浪费在与控制无关的外观细节上。LaST1.0将操作世界建模重构为潜空间中的控制中心未来预测，利用未来腕部视角的紧凑几何感知潜变量监督机器人-物体交互。模型采用无视觉编码器设计和LaST-Attention，统一建模跨模态时空关系。在RLBench、LIBERO和LIBERO-Plus等基准上取得领先成功率并展现泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: World-Action Models couple action learning with future prediction, enabling robotic policies to capture environmental dynamics for robust control. However, prevailing methods take a reconstruction-oriented approach to model future videos, allocating substantial capacity to appearance details that are incidental to control. In this work, we reformulate world modeling for manipulation as control-centric future prediction in latent space, and present LaST1.0, a unified latent World-Action Model. Rather than modeling an observation-complete video future, LaST1.0 predicts compact, geometry-aware latent targets derived from future wrist views, focusing the supervision on the evolving robot-object interactions required for fine-grained manipulation. To better support this control-centric paradigm, LaST1.0 revisits the visual input interface and attention mechanism of its unified architecture. It adopts a vision-encoder-free design with a lightweight patch embedder, exposing fine-grained visual cues directly to the backbone, and introduces LaST-Attention for structured spatiotemporal interactions across modalities. Evaluations across two robot embodiments, five challenging manipulation tasks, and three simulation benchmarks---RLBench, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus---demonstrate that LaST1.0 achieves state-of-the-art success rates and generalizes to novel scenarios. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of control-centric latent world modeling for robust manipulation.

papers.title_en: JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control
papers.authors: Xianhao Pan, Chi Li, Hanchao Li, Yunxin Liu, Jiankai Sun, Luhui Hu
papers.evidence: 双潜变量世界模型引导语言条件机器人控制策略
papers.tldr: 语言引导机器人控制中，指令应影响动作选择，却不应改变固定动作在相同观测下的预测后果。JEPA Dots用分离的动力学与任务表示构建紧凑双潜世界模型，以语言任务特征引导flow-matching策略，并用掩码注意力隔离指令无关的世界预测。在40个LIBERO任务闭环评估中总体成功率达84.9%，仅约39.1M参数，LIBERO-Goal从67.1%升至88.5%。该设计实现任务条件与动力学预测的解耦，为语言引导控制提供高效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Predictive world models for language-guided robot control face a fundamental conditioning challenge: instructions should influence action selection without altering the predicted consequences of fixed actions under identical observations. To address this challenge, we introduce JEPA Dots (Dynamics-Oriented Task Separation), a compact dual-latent framework that jointly learns visual dynamics and language-guided control through separate dynamics and task representations. Language-conditioned task features guide a flow-matching policy, while masked attention restricts world prediction to instruction-independent dynamics history and supplied actions. In closed-loop evaluation on 40 trained LIBERO tasks, JEPA Dots achieves 84.9% overall success with approximately 39.1M parameters, compared with the published 78.7% of NanoVLA-S with 161.0M parameters under a different evaluation protocol. In the reference experiment, JEPA Dots also improves overall success from 76.0% for our task-ID-conditioned adaptation baseline to 84.9%, with LIBERO-Goal success increasing from 67.1% to 88.5%. Instruction-switching experiments further confirm that task representations and policy outputs respond to language changes, while dynamics representations and world predictions remain invariant under fixed observations and supplied actions.

papers.title_en: Adaptive Action Horizon Selection via Flow-Field Uncertainty
papers.authors: Idan Ben-Ami, Arnon Netzer, Sarah Keren, Idit Diamant
papers.evidence: 从VLA流场事后估计不确定性以自适应选择动作视野
papers.tldr: VLA 自适应执行需要可靠不确定性估计，但现有 AAC 依赖多次采样动作块，推理开销高且混淆策略多样性与轨迹内不确定性。DUAC 从预训练 VLA 的流向量场提取轨迹条件不确定性，利用流后验协方差和 Jacobian-vector 乘积，由单个动作块计算动作级分数。在 LIBERO 系列与 RoboCasa 上，基于 DUAC 的自适应动作视野选择取得较高成功率与低估计延迟。该工作将流向量场确立为高效、轨迹条件化的机器人决策不确定性来源。
papers.abstract_en: Reliable uncertainty estimates are important for adaptive execution in vision-language-action (VLA) models. Existing approaches such as Adaptive Action Chunking (AAC) estimate action entropy from multiple sampled action chunks, introducing additional inference cost and capturing both uncertainty within an action trajectory and diversity across alternative strategies. We introduce Divergence-based Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Action Chunking (DUAC), a post-hoc method that extracts trajectory-conditioned predictive uncertainty from the vector field of a pretrained VLA. Building on a closed-form flow-posterior covariance formulation, DUAC derives action-level uncertainty scores from a single generated chunk using Jacobian-vector products, without retraining or multiple endpoint samples. DUAC strongly correlates with AAC, while capturing distinct information: AAC measures global dispersion across sampled chunks, whereas DUAC measures local uncertainty around the trajectory selected for execution. Consequently, DUAC is less sensitive to diversity among distinct but valid action strategies. Across LIBERO, LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa, DUAC-based adaptive horizon selection performs favorably among the evaluated methods, combining strong task success with low uncertainty-estimation latency. These results establish the flow vector field as an efficient, trajectory-conditioned source of predictive uncertainty for robot decision making.

papers.title_en: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
papers.authors: Yupeng Zheng, Chaoyue Li, Linbo Wang, Xiang Li, Yuhang Zheng, Xiaotong Su, Songen Gu, Yichen Zhang, Zebin Xing, Shuai Tian, Jingxiang Guo, Jing Li, Zhiyong Zhao, Zhongpu Xia, Qichao Zhang, Haoran Li, Shuicheng Yan, Dongbin Zhao
papers.evidence: 世界-动作模型学习场景结构并预测机器人操作动作。
papers.tldr: 现有世界-动作模型多依赖重建导向视觉表征，对操作所需空间关系与物体状态变化强调不足，限制泛化。Phoenix以双教师蒸馏增强DINOv3的几何与时空语义，并用CS-VAE将特征压缩为保留场景布局的生成潜变量，联合预测外观潜变量与动作。约3.9万小时预训练后，单臂、双臂与灵巧操作仿真和真实基准达SOTA，LIBERO-Plus 94.8%、RoboTwin 2.0 C2R 72.4%。同时展现更强缩放收益、跨具身迁移与少样本适应。
papers.abstract_en: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining. Following benchmark-specific post-training, Phoenix achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-robot benchmarks spanning single-arm, bimanual, and dexterous manipulation. It demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations, achieving success rates of 94.8% on LIBERO-Plus and 72.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, alongside strong cross-embodiment transfer and real-world manipulation performance on Bench2Dex and RoboDojo-RealWorld, respectively. Pretraining-scale analysis shows larger performance gains from data scaling than a video-VAE-only baseline, indicating stronger scaling benefits and more effective data utilization. Moreover, Phoenix maintains high success rates when adapted with limited downstream demonstrations, demonstrating strong few-shot adaptation. Our code, pretraining data, and models are available on the project page to help the community reproduce our results.

papers.title_en: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
papers.authors: Chenyuan Zhou, Chaoyi Huang, Zibo Wang, Zhiyuan Li, Yong-Lu Li
papers.evidence: 具身智能体结合VLA策略实现工具自适应操作
papers.tldr: 不同形状工具可能功能相似，但跨工具迁移操作技能需理解几何与任务关系并调整策略。A²-VLA将工具可供性视为可构建、测试和修正的假设，用具身智能体在仿真重建场景中自主发现功能区域及关键几何特征，并通过实验积累可复用提取技能。该方法以功能区域编码条件化π₀.₅策略，在仿真跨工具轨迹重定向中达86.1%成功率，真实机器人三任务较π₀.₅提升30.7个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: Tools with different shapes can have similar functions, but transferring manipulation skills across tools requires understanding how tool geometry relates to the specific task and adjusting the manipulation strategy accordingly. The key challenge is to discover the common affordances that contribute to task completion across different tools and verify whether they support new tools in performing similar work. We present A$^2$-VLA, a tool-adaptation framework that combines an embodied agent with a VLA policy. It treats tool affordances as hypotheses the agent can construct, test, and revise. Given teleoperated demonstrations with a few source tools, the agent reconstructs the scenes in simulation and autonomously determines task-relevant affordance features: functional regions and their key geometric properties. It develops affordance-extraction skills and refines both the features and skills through autonomous experiments in the reconstructed scenes. Validated extraction skills accumulate in a reusable skill library for unseen tools. Finally, A$^2$-VLA uses encoded functional-region features as conditioning inputs to a $π_{0.5}$ backbone during training and inference. Evaluation examines affordance reliability in reconstructed scenes and real-robot task success on unseen tools. Our method achieves 86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting based on affordances. On three real-robot tool-use tasks, A$^2$-VLA improves task success by 30.7 percentage points over $π_{0.5}$.

papers.title_en: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
papers.authors: Zheyuan Liu, Chuhan Wang, Jinduo Guo, Yue Huang, Xiangchi Yuan, Ningshan Ma, Meng Jiang
papers.evidence: 面向安全机器人控制与停止被禁行为的VLA模型
papers.tldr: VLA模型能依据视觉与语言指令执行多样任务，但执行中途停止违规行为并控制物理反应仍困难；仅从初始状态抑制任务，接管后仍可能完成，且可能掉落物体。SAFI采用回退目标构建与联合策略适配两阶段，在禁止任务演示中设定静止手臂和一致夹爪目标，并与保留任务动作联合学习。在LIBERO/BadLIBERO上，接管后目标成功率降至1.3%，无物理事故与动作饱和，保留任务成功率仍高。该工作把安全停止从“拒绝任务”推进到执行中状态感知的安全回退。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging. Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution. Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety. To address these challenges, we introduce State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response. SAFI comprises two stages, (1) fallback target construction, which assigns stationary arm commands and consistent gripper targets throughout prohibited-task demonstrations, and (2) joint policy adaptation, which learns these targets alongside the original actions of retained tasks. This supervision teaches an explicit alternative response at intermediate execution states while maintaining the robot's other skills. Extensive experiments with OpenVLA-OFT across LIBERO and BadLIBERO tasks evaluate prohibited completion, physical incidents, and retained-task performance. On the evaluated LIBERO tasks, SAFI reduces aggregate target success after takeover to 1.3\%, with no recorded physical incidents or action saturation, while preserving high retained-task success.

papers.title_en: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Zilang Cen, Chao Tang, Fangcheng Liu, Weishi Mi, Wei Hao, JiaYu Xu, Dehao Huang, Yehui Tang, Xiaohui Cui, Tingguang Li, Xiaoyuan Zhang
papers.evidence: 协调高层多模态推理智能体与底层机器人控制策略
papers.tldr: 长程机器人操作中，大模型频繁调用带来高延迟与高 token 成本，且难判断何时需要智能体介入及该修复执行还是重规划。RoC 通过在线任务状态监测器融合时序视觉与有序交互记忆，估计当前子任务进度并预测后继子任务，以事件触发方式调用高层推理智能体，协同执行修复与计划修订。在 RMBench 上，任务成功率较最强智能体基线提升 24.0 个百分点，token 消耗降低 65.3%，并较最强策略基线提升 15.1 个百分点；真实世界三项长程任务也验证有效。
papers.abstract_en: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

papers.title_en: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
papers.authors: Weile Li, Yunfan Lou, Muqing Shi, Zihao Zhang, Zhenbiao Huang, Boxian Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Zhibo Pang
papers.evidence: 融合触觉感知的视觉-语言-动作模型用于接触丰富操作
papers.tldr: 视觉-语言-动作模型加入触觉后收益不稳定，因为部分触觉变化可由视觉和执行动作预测。TacInno将视觉与动作无法解释的接触动力学单独定义为触觉创新，并用条件化tokenizer压缩未来触觉变化为离散码，仅作为训练目标。TacInno-VLA在六个仿真任务平均成功率87.5%，四个真实任务70.5%，分别超最强基线10.7和9.0个百分点。该工作表明触觉创新可作为接触丰富操作的有效监督信号。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.
